items.fullText: Nov 26th, 2026 Marc Levinson on How UPS Created Modern Logistics UPS was founded nearly a century ago in the basement of a Seattle saloon by James E. Casey and his business partner Claude Ryan. It is now hard to imagine modern, globalized life, and the logistics required to prop it up, without the innovations Casey and his partners at UPS cooked up during the company's early decades. Marc Levinson has just written a biography of Casey and the company he founded — UPS Man: James E. Casey and the Creation of Modern Logistics — which was a lot harder to do than you might imagine, because Casey shunned the spotlight and his contributions were virtually unknown outside of UPS. In today's episode, Levinson tells us why UPS is so secretive about its history, how Casey and his partners helped figure out the last mile problem and popularized parcel delivery, and how scientific management theories influenced everything the company did. Anthropic’s Stock Sparks Divide Inside One Wall Street Firm
items.d: Two equity analysts at a single Wall Street research firm have taken the unusual step of posting conflicting views on the outlook for the hottest stock in the market: Anthropic PBC’s newly listed shares.
items.fullText: Technology Anthropic’s Stock Sparks Divide Inside One Wall Street Firm Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Expand Anthropic signage during the company's IPO at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York on Nov. 19. Photographer: John Lamparski/Bloomberg Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Gift this article Contact us: Provide news feedback or report an error Confidential tip? Send a tip to our reporters Site feedback: Take our Survey New Window Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift By Henry Ren November 25, 2026 at 9:35 PM UTC Updated on November 26, 2026 at 9:08 AM UTC Bookmark Save Takeaways by Bloomberg AI Two equity analysts at a single Wall Street research firm have taken the unusual step of posting conflicting views on the outlook for the hottest stock in the market: Anthropic PBC ’s newly listed shares. On one side, Andrew Freedman , a communications and software analyst at Hedgeye Risk Management , has put out reports since the company’s initial public offering and said in an interview on Wednesday that the stock is trading at levels that should be attractive for long-term investors. Meanwhile, his colleague Felix Wang , a global tech analyst, sent out a note to clients on Tuesday, recommending they short the stock.

items.fullText: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents See how developers are combining AI agents with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, test physical behavior and guide improvements. November 19, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nyhamna_footage_take5_30s.mp4 AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation.
